title: Modular Commerce
readerIntent: Understand how separate commerce authorities compose one customer experience.
priorKnowledge: Understand tenants, enterprises, catalogs, publishing, cache, and search.
owner: Storefront, Store, Product, Pricing, Inventory, Units, and publishing capability owners
summary: Nodics composes website context, stores, products, prices, and stock at runtime while each capability retains its own schemas, services, policies, publishing, and operational authority.

sections.heading: Why separate authorities matter
items: A product can exist without a price or current stock.
Prices vary by enterprise, website, store, country, channel, segment, customer, quantity, currency, and time.
Stock belongs to warehouse/pool balances and sourcing policy, not the product record.
Storefront resolves trusted website context but does not own Store, CMS, Pricing, or Inventory data.
Units provide reusable measurement semantics without becoming a commerce business service.

sections.heading: Commerce journey
items: Resolve hostname to Storefront Site and trusted context.
Load the applicable content and product catalogs.
Resolve Product identity and merchandising data.
Resolve the best eligible Price from governed scopes and priority.
Source available Stock from eligible warehouses/pools and units.
Serve online projections from cache/search while authoritative modules remain recoverable.
